ety.text: First recorded in 1820 by A. A. Uspensky in the Fenya argot of Vladimir with the meaning 'noble' (provided клювый (kljuvyj) in the "Suzdal dialect" by Pallas in 1787 is a misprint or typo instead of *кліовый). From the second half of the 19th century, it also appears in thieves' argot. According to Preobrazhensky's suggestion, supported by Vasmer, it comes from the verb клевать (klevatʹ) (further from Proto-Slavic *kľьvati, from which originated, among others: Old Church Slavonic кльвати (klĭvati), perfective клюнѫти (kljunǫti), Ukrainian клювати (kljuvaty), Belarusian клюваць (kljuvacʹ), Bul…
